2. Plaintiff then obtained rule and at the time of hearing of the revisional application his learned advocate took the ground that though an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act was filed by the defendant-appellant in the lower appellate court for condoning the delay of 147 days, yet the lower appellate court decided the appeal without disposing of the said application and as such the judgment and decree of the lower appellate court must be set aside on this ground alone. The High Court Division rejecting the said submission considered the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act on merit and came to the finding that there were sufficient grounds to condone the delay and accordingly condoned the delay. The High Court Division upon a lengthy discussion also came to the conclusion that the lower appellate court was right in allowing the appeal and dismissing the suit on merit. 

 3. Leaned Advocate for the plaintiff-leave petitioner submits only one ground that the High Court Division erred in law in affirming the judgment and decree of the lower appellate court in view of the fact that the lower appellate court failed to consider and decide the question of limitation and that the High Court Division ought not to have decided the question of limitation by pre-empting the function of the lower appellate court.
